correctness.rationale: For every c, an approving voter is unrepresented iff its interval is entirely inside the consecutive selected-candidate gap containing c; elected candidates have zero uncovered support. Therefore all quota-JR committees correspond bijectively to gap-admissible increasing paths, and the suffix recurrence counts exactly. Precomputation complexity and O(m)-bit count bound hold. Tested 320,546 exhaustive DR cases, 12,000 general random cases versus an independently written direct predicate.

value.rationale: The exact number of JR committees was formulated as a natural #P-hard counting problem in Bredereck et al. (2019); computing it allows quantitative comparison of fairness restrictions. Here a structurally meaningful candidate-interval restriction yields polynomial exact counts, exact uniform sampling, and a DR corollary with candidate eligibility fixed by the new DR axiom. This is not merely existence or a known-table recomputation.
